correctness.rationale: For every d>=3, degree-3 products of three F_2-lines avoiding an individual rational Fano point are the seven point-indicator sections; multiplication by a nonvanishing linear form to degree d makes evaluation V_d -> F_2^7 surjective, kernel dimension N_d-7. The eligible seven-bit 2-spaces were enumerated independently from all seven incidence lines: exactly 287, with zero-locus profiles (1,2,4):21, (1,3,3):42, (2,2,3):84, (2,3,4):84, (3,3,3):56, and common rational basepoint sizes 0:147, 1:140. Every eligible pencil is exactly a graph U -> ker(ev_d), giving 287*2^(2(N_d-7)) in all degrees, the indicated profile/basepoint multiplicities, and limiting fraction 861/8192. An independent second finite enumeration of all 1024 degree-3 binary masks and 168 invertible linear changes produced 18,368 cubic pencils, 112 projective orbits of sizes 168*108 plus 56*4, and 784 all-geometrically-smooth pencils in six orbits; exact characteristic-2 Macaulay rank 15 checked smoothness, yielding smooth-member distribution (4816,9408,3360,784). The all-degree argument is algebraic, not extrapolated from cubic enumeration. The seven Fano incidence classes, PGL action and Macaulay rank criterion were reconstructed from frozen code and independent enumeration. No geometric smoothness requirement attaches to the all-degree theorem.

value.rationale: An exact all-degree quantitative solution to a natural nonblocking-pencil existence problem over the smallest projective plane: the sharp 287 incidence patterns induce an all-d formula and limiting fraction 861/8192, while the possible common rational base locus is completely classified. The complete cubic orbit and smooth-member stratifications answer a separate natural embedded-linear-system symmetry question. These are unknown, non-automatic geometric/combinatorial invariants of motivated objects, rather than arbitrary numerical slices.

limitations: All-degree pencil count imposes only rational-member nonblocking; it does not require geometric smoothness. The 112-orbit census is cubic only, and any prior all-smooth-pencil result is credited rather than repackaged.
